head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: Scope: all 41 manifest files read in full; no partners. Known-ledger entries not re-reported (security-MAJ-4-r1 additionalDirectories reconcile, security-MIN-3-r2 policy-guard path matching, correctness-MAJ-24-r1 removed acdsl ask rules, correctness-MAJ-10-r2 unquoted install.env). Examined and dropped as non-exploits or out-of-direction: skill-invoke-gate/read-gate fail-open paths (agent-conduct gates, no attacker input); install.sh PEEK_*_HOME interpolated unescaped into sed/plist XML (operator-supplied only); .serena/.DS_Store exclusions and squash containment as removal grounds in remove_agent_worktrees.sh / worktree-sessionstart.sh (possible loss of untracked .serena memories — data-integrity, not security); bootstrap token handling (token exported to env, never logged). No runtime probes: the lane contract forbids running scripts via bash, so evidence is static. CROSS-CHUNK for the station: (1) install.env is sourced as shell code by install.sh and sync_settings.sh; the header says the Go configserver -install also writes it — if any configserver HTTP path writes PEEK_*_HOME into install.env unquoted, a localhost request (CSRF-reachable) becomes command execution on the next sync; verify the Go writer quotes/validates. (2) Casual profile now defaults orchestrate=1 and auto-apply=decide in routines/smine-nightly/run.sh, so mined proposals can be auto-applied, merged to main and synced into ~/.claude/hooks and settings without a human gate (known BLK-8-r2 says orchestrate runs sync_settings.sh); whether skills/smine-orchestrate and auto-apply-rules.md refuse changes to cmd/hooks/** and settings/** is outside this chunk.

findings.fix: Register acdsl-policy-guard.sh under a Bash matcher too and, for tool_name Bash, deny when a command token (read-gate's conservative tokenizer) resolves under $root to the self-management surface (or, in strict mode, to *.acdsl / acdsl/*); alternatively drop Bash(cp *) from the template allow list.
findings.claim: The acdsl policy guard only sees Write/Edit/NotebookEdit file paths, while the deployed settings template auto-allows Bash(cp *) under acceptEdits, so in a repo whose acdsl/policy.json is strict or gated an agent overwrites acdsl/policy.json (or any rule file in strict mode) with one Bash call and receives neither a deny nor a permission prompt.
findings.evidence: Re-read cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh:12-14 — file_path is taken from tool_input.file_path // tool_input.notebook_path and the hook exits 0 when it is empty, so a Bash payload (tool_input.command only) is never evaluated. Re-read settings/claude_code/settings.json:203-216 — the guard is registered only under matcher "Write|Edit|NotebookEdit"; settings.json:16 allow-lists "Bash(cp *)" and :110 sets defaultMode acceptEdits. Sequence: repo with acdsl/policy.json {"mode":"strict"}; agent runs `cp /tmp/p.json acdsl/policy.json` (1 attempt, 0 prompts, 0 cost) — the PreToolUse guard never runs and the allow rule admits the call; the same `cp x.acdsl acdsl/rules.acdsl` defeats the strict-mode rule-file lock. Exposure rare: this repo ships mode free (acdsl/policy.json:2), only repos running gated/strict (dist_mode gated) are affected. Effect held at degraded, not destructive: the hook header (lines 4-6) states acdsl check CheckPolicy is the authoritative judge, which lives outside this chunk and was not verified — the hook's fast-feedback layer is what is lost. Distinct from known security-MIN-3-r2 (path normalization / cwd root on Write/Edit): this is the uncovered Bash tool, not path matching. No runtime probe: the lane contract forbids running scripts with bash.
